hook: Andrew Feldman has built two companies around the same conviction, that general-purpose processors are the wrong tool for specialized workloads. He first proved it with SeaMicro, a microserver startup he founded in 2007 that AMD acquired in 2012 for roughly 334 million dollars. He then co-founded Cerebras Systems in 2015 to apply the same logic to AI, building the Wafer-Scale Engine, a single chip roughly the size of a dinner plate designed specifically to keep AI training data close to compute instead of shuttling it between separate processors. As Cerebras CEO, Feldman has positioned wafer-scale computing as an alternative to clusters of GPUs for large-scale AI training and inference.

quick_facts: Co-founder and CEO of Cerebras Systems, founded in 2015 with Gary Lauterbach, Michael James, Sean Lie, and Jean-Philippe Fricker
Cerebras built the Wafer-Scale Engine, a single chip built for AI training and inference rather than general-purpose computing
Previously founded SeaMicro in 2007, a maker of energy-efficient microserver technology for cloud data centers
AMD acquired SeaMicro in February 2012 for approximately 334 million dollars
Served as General Manager of AMD's Data Center Server Solutions business following the SeaMicro acquisition
